messages:
incident-bot: Deploy monitor detected elevated 5xx rate in canary (us-west-2) for /v1/generate - 12m window: p95 latency up, 5xx spike ~18% vs baseline 0.8%. Auto-abort threshold crossed. link: https://internal.ops/reports/1764509876
alex: saw the alert, pulling canary logs now. any obvious errors?
maria: logs show repeated TLS handshake timeouts and upstream 502s from model-proxy-1/2. Also healthcheck failures on 3/10 canary instances.
jordan: confirming traffic split was 5% to canary for this rollout. did the new routing policy change headers?
amodeling: (reacts :eyes:)
alex: not sure yet, but canary instances show `kvcache miss` warnings too. possible mismatch with quantized runtime?
maria: runbook says first step: pause rollout and reduce traffic to 0. Triggering feature-flag kill.
alex: pausing rollout via deploy service... `kubectl annotate rollout redwood/model-serving rollout-paused=true`
incident-bot: Rollout pause acknowledged by deployer at 1764509902. Canary traffic reduced to 0.
jordan: initiating feature flag kill: `featureflag rollback model-routing-v2`
sam: doing the kill now — flag updated, waiting for config propagation (estimated ~30s).
incident-bot: Feature flag flipped at 1764509938; routing reverted to stable variant. Traffic to canary drained.
maria: good. next: assess customer impact. any user-facing 5xx spikes correlated? SLO dashboards show elevated 5xx on a handful of high-QPS routes, error budget hit ~3% for the minute window.
alex: quick check with metrics: internal API error rate returned to baseline ~2m after flag flip. No long-running user sessions reported as failed, but a few client retries observed.
jordan: sounds like partial impact for some requests — file an incident sev2 and notify support to watch major customers.
sam: filed ticket INC-2023 and pinged support channel. message sent to customer-success with suggested mitigation notes.
maria: root cause hypothesis: new routing policy introduced an extra TLS connection reuse layer that interacts poorly with the quantized runtime's connection pooling, causing handshake timeouts and transient 502s. We should roll back the routing change and open a deeper RCA.
alex: agree. scheduling a rollback of the routing policy in the next maintenance window unless we can reproduce and patch quickly.
jordan: for now, canary nodes are healthy again. continuing to monitor for 15m. handoff to night oncall in 20m.
sre-bot: On-call handoff reminder: @night-oncall set to jordan. Handoff notes: paused rollout, feature flag killed, traffic reverted, incident ticket INC-2023, hypothesis noted, monitoring watch.
jordan: taking oncall. if anything flares, escalate to eng-sre and paging list.
alex: quick checklist to capture before handoff: upload canary logs to /artifacts/1764509876, record model-proxy versions, and tag metrics dashboard with incident id.
maria: copying logs and attaching to INC-2023 now.
sam: adding runbook link and next steps: (1) full rollback of routing policy, (2) test connection pooling changes against quantized runtime, (3) postmortem in 48h.
jordan: ack. signed off and beginning monitoring window handoff. :white_check_mark:
incident-bot: Incident thread closed for primary responders at 1764510120. If issues recur, reopen with `open-incident` command.
